content.comment_body: Hello, I have a brand new [article_no]. When I try to send my program to the [product_name], [product_name] software always displays the error 'unable to access the remote device.' The software shows the device IP as 192.168.0.3, and when my PC's IP is 192.168.0.2 I can ping it successfully. I have tried connecting via both ethernet ports directly and also through a switch/router with both static IP and DHCP, but still get the same error. Has anyone found a solution for this issue? Best wishes, [user_name]

It sounds like you are using [product_name] software version V8.2.x or older, while your [product_name] hardware is a newer [version_no] model. You need [product_name] V8.3 for it to work. The upgrade is available for download, but is subject to export restrictions. You will need to complete additional registration steps to access restricted software.
I'm experiencing the same issue, could someone help us resolve it?
If your problem matches, please refer to the links mentioned in my previous post.
I'm having the exact same problem. What's the solution?
If your issue is identical, please check the references in the previous post above yours.
Okay :) I'm still waiting for my registration inquiry to be processed.
I'm waiting as well—my registration process is still pending.

I'm also facing the same problem. I can see the [product_name] device when I click refresh at 192.168.0.3 (my PC is at 192.168.0.100). After selecting the device and clicking test, I get the 'unable to access the remote device' error. I tried on both Windows 7 and Windows 10 with the same result. I'm using [product_name] version 8.2.1 (which is outdated). Can anyone assist, please?
Thanks. Upgrading to [product_name] v8.3 resolved it for me—I was able to connect successfully.

Hello, I'm currently facing the same issue. 1) Installed [product_name] 8.3. 2) The refresh button locates the device at IP 192.168.0.3. 3) The connect button does not work: 'Unable to access the remote device.' My setup is a Windows 10 PC with both automatic and manual IP, using [product_name] [article_no]. As a note, older [product_name] like [article_no] connect without problems. Thanks in advance,
The [product_name] device requires a fixed IP address. If connecting through a router with DHCP, make sure the IP address is outside the DHCP range.

Thanks for your reply! The [product_name] has a fixed IP and connects via ethernet to the PC. Notably, the older [product_name] connects fine with the same IP address (192.168.0.3). I tried assigning another IP outside of the DHCP range, but it still didn't work (as shown in the image attached). Thank you in advance,
Have you tried assigning a different IP address to the [product_name] device?
Yes, I have. The screenshot attached to my previous post shows that I assigned IP 192.168.0.250 to the [product_name] device. Is this the correct approach? Thank you in advance. Regards,
What are the IP address, subnet mask, and gateway address used by your PC?

Based on my 'ipconfig' output (see attached image): Ethernet Adapter: DNS suffix: IPv6 address: IPv4 address: 192.168.0.254 Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0 Gateway: It appears there is no gateway address. Regards,

You've updated the screenshot. The first shows two ethernet adapters—one with IPv4 = 192.168.0.71, subnet mask = 255.255.255.0, gateway = 192.168.0.254, and the other with IPv4 = 192.168.0.254, subnet mask = 255.255.255.0, gateway = 0.0.0.0. Not sure which connection you are using.

Yes, I changed the screenshot to focus on the ethernet connection relevant to the [product_name] (IP: 192.168.0.254). I tried different IP addresses for the device and found that 192.168.0.150 works. This implies previous addresses were likely already in use. It's peculiar that the older [product_name] works even with an already assigned IP like 192.168.0.3. Thanks for your assistance and support—it was very helpful! Regards,

Is it still necessary for the [product_name] device to have an IP outside the DHCP range? If so, that's a major problem for industrial setups. My [product_name] and software version 8.3 can detect the device but can't download to it, which took all day to discover. We might not be able to use it in our environment.

Is it still a requirement for the [product_name] device IP to be outside the DHCP range? That's a major inconvenience for industrial installations. My [product_name] hardware and [product_name] software v8.3 can see the device but cannot transfer the program. The router assigns DHCP addresses, and fixed IPs within the DHCP range aren't tracked by the router, so requests sent to these IPs can't be forwarded properly.

Other devices don't have this issue—we have hundreds of fixed IP units in our facility. After assigning a fixed IP, the router or switch checks if it's free, then assigns it to the device. This is true for many manufacturers. This issue seems unique to this [company_name] device; it's our first [product_name] test, and it did not go well. Usually, network devices check for IP conflicts using a broadcast query.

Is this limitation only for programming? Can we still communicate via Modbus, or between devices if the IP falls in the DHCP range? If so, it might be workable—we'd just need to connect directly for programming, which is inconvenient but manageable. Does anyone have clarity on this?

Hello, I'm experiencing similar problems using [product_name] 8.3 and the latest hardware, configured with a fixed IP and a project loaded. I cannot connect to view the project and constantly get the error. I am connected directly from my laptop to the BM with both in the same subnet. Thanks in advance. Regards, [user_name]
How are the [product_name] and laptop connected? Directly or on a network with a router? What are the IP address and subnet mask for both devices?
Hello, The devices are directly connected with an ethernet cable: [product_name] at 192.168.203.56, PC at 192.168.203.100, and both use subnet mask 255.255.255.0. Regards, [user_name]
If the [product_name] and laptop are only directly connected and not part of a network, that's unusual.
Hello [user_name], Have you tried pinging the [product_name]? What do the status LEDs on the network ports indicate? Have you tested with an IP scanner? [user_name] (translated with Google)

Hi [user_name], Yes, I've pinged the device and it replies every time; the status lights are flashing. I'm also having trouble accessing the unit via Modbus, likely due to the same underlying problem.
Please don't post multiple times for the same issue. You've also opened a separate topic: Modbus Communications Issues Over Network.

Hi, I didn't mean to double post—I responded to the original thread about ping and network lights, then added additional info regarding the Modbus issue as they might be related. Disabling DHCP in this context seems counterintuitive—it's quite challenging in industrial environments. We've never encountered this with similar equipment before, and I suspect this is the root of our issues. Cheers,

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users repeatedly encounter difficulties connecting to [product_name] hardware using [product_name] software, frequently seeing a 'unable to access the remote device' error. The core issue appears to be version incompatibility—connecting newer [version_no] hardware with older software versions. While users confirm network connectivity and proper hardware setup, access is denied unless the correct software version is installed. Additionally, the software upgrade requires export registration, leading to user frustration and delays.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect hardware and software from [company_name] to work together seamlessly, without additional registration steps or software upgrade restrictions. They anticipate a straightforward experience when connecting and programming [product_name] devices, especially when network connectivity is established.
